signal: Today’s strongest signal is that the frontier is compressing into the runtime and post-training stack: OpenAI and Anthropic are pushing high-end capability into cheaper models with cache economics tuned for long-lived agents, Xiaomi is opening both weights and large-scale RL machinery, defenders are seeing autonomy move into malware control loops, and inference research is aligning draft-model training directly with serving-time acceptance.

stories.title: OpenAI pushes GPT-6 intelligence into cheaper Sol and Luna tiers with agent-friendly caching
stories.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, saying both were trained with methods similar to GPT-6 Astra and bring its advances in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use and alignment into lower-cost tiers. Standard API prices are $2 input and $10 output per million tokens for Sol and $0.10 input and $0.50 output for Luna, 50% below GPT-5.6 promotional pricing. OpenAI also upgraded GPT-6 prompt caching so reasoning-effort and tool-availability changes can preserve reusable context; cached input reads can receive a 90% discount, and GitHub reports that the new caching reduced fresh prompt processing by more than 50% across billions of Copilot requests.
stories.whyItMatters: Persistent agents spend heavily on repeated instructions, tool schemas and accumulated context, so cache behavior is becoming part of model economics rather than a minor API optimization. Lower model prices plus cache stability across changes in reasoning effort and tool availability make long-running coding and workflow agents easier to route dynamically. Teams should benchmark cost per accepted task with their real cache-hit distribution, not compare provider sticker prices in isolation.
stories.attention: Very high — frontier-class capability is being pushed into lower-cost production tiers while caching becomes part of the agent execution contract

stories.title: Anthropic launches Opus 5.5 with Fable-level capability, cheaper cache reads and stronger safety testing
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in its 5.5 family, and says it performs at Claude Fable 5.1 level on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5. The model is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, with cache reads cut to $0.20 per million and output generation more than 30% faster than Opus 5. Anthropic also says Opus 5.5 is its strongest model yet on its automated behavioral audit, with improved prompt-injection resistance, and had Frontier Design and METR evaluate it before release.
stories.whyItMatters: For coding and research agents, cache-read pricing, output speed and token efficiency increasingly dominate total workflow cost. The release also shows safety evaluation moving closer to the same long-horizon agent workloads that drive capability: external review, prompt-injection resistance and boundary-following are becoming release criteria alongside benchmarks. Anthropic’s performance numbers are vendor-reported, so production evaluation should still use your own repositories and task traces.
stories.attention: Very high — the capability-versus-cost frontier is moving quickly, and long-horizon safety is becoming part of model-release engineering

stories.title: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo-V2.6 and the RL stack behind a trillion-parameter multimodal agent model
stories.summary: Xiaomi MiMo released and open-sourced MiMo-V2.6 Pro and Flash after a six-day large-scale reinforcement-learning run spanning code, general-agent, visual and cybersecurity tasks. Xiaomi reports roughly 750,000 training trajectories and says the Pro run cost about $2.62 million; its open model card describes Pro as a 1.02-trillion-parameter sparse MoE with 42 billion active parameters, a 1M-token context window and text, image, video and audio input. The release includes model weights, a technical report, RL code, 7,000-plus task environments and a lightweight composable harness.
stories.whyItMatters: The high-signal part is the training substrate, not only another open checkpoint. Xiaomi is exposing mixed-domain RL, large-batch asynchronous optimization, grader scaling, reward-hacking defenses and multi-harness training alongside the weights, which gives teams something concrete to reproduce and modify. Vendor benchmark gains still need independent validation, but an open post-training stack can accelerate research on agent RL far more than weights alone.
stories.attention: Very high — a strong open-weight release is arriving with unusually complete agent-RL infrastructure and training artifacts

stories.title: Cisco Talos finds a Windows implant that lets four LLMs vote on its next attack action
stories.summary: Cisco Talos disclosed CLOSEDQUORUM, a Windows implant that can ask DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Gemini to vote on the next tactical action and then execute the winning typed decision. The action schema is constrained to capabilities such as credential theft, process injection and persistence. Talos has not confirmed in-the-wild deployment, and the public distribution sample contains placeholder API keys and a dummy webhook, so the analyzed build is not an observed live campaign. The work was released alongside CAIRN, Talos’ open-source toolkit for tracking AI-integrated malware.
stories.whyItMatters: The design is more important than the maturity of this specific binary: autonomous reasoning can replace parts of a traditional command-and-control loop without requiring an attacker to stay online. Defenders should correlate AI-provider traffic with process behavior, credential access, persistence and exfiltration rather than block model-provider domains in isolation. Agent security has a mirror image on the offensive side: typed actions, bounded choices and tool orchestration also make malicious autonomy easier to engineer.
stories.attention: Very high — autonomous LLM control loops are appearing inside malware architectures even if this public sample is still a prototype

stories.title: Speculative-decoding research trains draft models for accepted tokens instead of distribution matching
stories.summary: A new speculative-decoding paper argues that draft models should be trained directly for verification acceptance rather than mainly through cross-entropy or KL divergence. The authors derive an Expected Accepted Length objective for greedy decoding and a Window Total Variation objective for sampling-based decoding, both of which target the expected number of accepted tokens across the speculative window. They can also add a GRPO stage using simulated acceptance length as reward, and report consistent acceptance-length improvements over KL-based training across multiple target and draft models, tasks and decoding settings.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a clean example of training-serving co-design: the draft model is not useful because it imitates the target distribution in the abstract, but because it produces tokens the verifier will actually accept. The right objective also depends on the production decoding mode. Teams building speculative stacks should therefore train against the acceptance policy, temperature and speculative window they will deploy, rather than optimizing a generic imitation loss and hoping throughput follows.
stories.attention: High — speculative decoding is moving from proxy-trained draft models toward objectives matched directly to serving-time acceptance

takeaway: Treat model price, cacheability, post-training provenance, action authority and serving objectives as one engineering system. Route work by cost per accepted outcome, structure long-lived context for reuse, prefer releases whose training artifacts can be audited, detect autonomous tooling by behavior rather than provider domains, and train inference helpers against the exact runtime metric they are meant to improve.
